proofs.proof_tex:
Write \(\|V\|_2=\{E_P\|V\|^2\}^{1/2}\), with the Euclidean, Frobenius, or operator norm according to the type of \(V\).  Constants below depend only on the quantities allowed in \(C_{\mathrm{reg}}\).  By the support-cleaning lemma,
\[
 \|\bar M_A-M_A\|_2\leq C_{\mathrm{reg}}r_A^c,
 \qquad
 \|\bar M_Z-M_Z\|_2\leq C_{\mathrm{reg}}r_Z^c.                 \tag{41}
\]
These bounds hold whether or not the screening event occurs; that event is needed for exact recovery of zeros, not for stability.

Put
\[
 H=B^{\mathsf T}D^{-1}B,
 \qquad
 \widehat H=\widehat B^{\mathsf T}\widehat D^{-1}\widehat B,
 \qquad
 \widehat B=\bar M_A\odot\bar M_Z.                              \tag{42}
\]
Observed-cell positivity gives \(\|D^{-1}\|_{\mathrm{op}}\leq\varepsilon^{-1}\), and the computable fitted half-margin gives \(\|\widehat D^{-1}\|_{\mathrm{op}}\leq2\varepsilon^{-1}\).  For \(v\in\mathbb R^K\), matricization and the Khatri--Rao definition yield
\[
 \operatorname{mat}(Bv)=M_A\operatorname{diag}(v)M_Z^{\mathsf T},
 \qquad
 \operatorname{mat}(\widehat Bv)=\bar M_A\operatorname{diag}(v)\bar M_Z^{\mathsf T}. \tag{43}
\]
The true singular-value margins and the fitted half-margins therefore imply
\[
 \|Bv\|_2\geq\varepsilon^2\|v\|_2,
 \qquad
 \|\widehat Bv\|_2\geq\frac{\varepsilon^2}{4}\|v\|_2.          \tag{44}
\]
Since the diagonal entries of \(D\) and \(\widehat D\) are probabilities and hence at most one,
\[
 v^{\mathsf T}Hv=\|D^{-1/2}Bv\|_2^2\geq\varepsilon^4\|v\|_2^2,
 \qquad
 v^{\mathsf T}\widehat Hv\geq\frac{\varepsilon^4}{16}\|v\|_2^2.
\]
Thus both matrices are invertible and
\[
 \|H^{-1}\|_{\mathrm{op}}\leq\varepsilon^{-4},
 \qquad
 \|\widehat H^{-1}\|_{\mathrm{op}}\leq16\varepsilon^{-4}.      \tag{45}
\]

The exact identities
\[
 \widehat D^{-1}-D^{-1}=\widehat D^{-1}(D-\widehat D)D^{-1},
 \qquad
 \widehat H^{-1}-H^{-1}=\widehat H^{-1}(H-\widehat H)H^{-1}      \tag{46}
\]
and product telescoping in \(B^{\mathsf T}D^{-1}B\) give
\[
 \|\widehat H-H\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 \leq C_{\mathrm{reg}}
 \bigl(\|\widehat B-B\|_{\mathrm{op}}+\|\widehat D-D\|_{\mathrm{op}}\bigr). \tag{47}
\]
Applying (46)--(47) to
\[
 N_B=I_{K^2}-D^{-1}BH^{-1}B^{\mathsf T},
 \qquad
 \widehat N=I_{K^2}-\widehat D^{-1}\widehat B\widehat H^{-1}\widehat B^{\mathsf T}
\]
gives pointwise
\[
 \|\widehat N-N_B\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 \leq C_{\mathrm{reg}}
 \bigl(\|\widehat D-D\|_{\mathrm{op}}+\|\widehat B-B\|_{\mathrm{op}}\bigr). \tag{48}
\]
Taking the declared conditional \(L^2(P)\) norm proves the first displayed assertion.

The cleaned inverse-feature bridges satisfy the exact identities
\[
 \bar M_A^{-1}M_A-I_K=\bar M_A^{-1}(M_A-\bar M_A),
 \qquad
 \bar M_Z^{-1}M_Z-I_K=\bar M_Z^{-1}(M_Z-\bar M_Z).               \tag{49}
\]
The fitted singular-value half-margins and (41) consequently bound the two conditional bridge-mean errors by \(C_{\mathrm{reg}}r_A^c\) and \(C_{\mathrm{reg}}r_Z^c\).  The fitted outcome regression is not an independently chosen nuisance: bounded support and its definition from \(\widehat f\) give \(|\widehat m_j|\leq L\).  Product telescoping in the raw bridge formula, latent positivity, and the fitted propensity half-margin then give
\[
 \|\widehat U-U\|_2
 \leq C_{\mathrm{reg}}(r_m+r_\pi+r_A^c+r_Z^c)
 \leq C_{\mathrm{reg}}R_\Sigma.                                \tag{50}
\]

For the conditional Gram step, the established data-driven Gram-threshold lemma, applied with \(\tau_G=\varepsilon/2\), yields
\[
 \|\widehat G_{\tau_G}^{\dagger}-G^+\|_{L^2(P_X;\mathrm{op})}
 \leq26\varepsilon^{-2}r_G,
 \qquad
 \|\widehat G_{\tau_G}^{\dagger}\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 \leq2\varepsilon^{-1}.                                        \tag{51}
\]
Every map preceding this solve is evaluated at the cleaned product law.  Conditional expectation is an \(L^2\)-contraction, and the inverse identity (46), its measurement analogue (49), and finite product telescoping show successively that the errors of \(\widehat B,\widehat d,\widehat D,\widehat R,\widehat N,\widehat c,\widehat h,\widehat G\), and \(\widehat b_{(\cdot)}\) are precisely the cleaned-law coordinates \(r_B,r_d,r_D,r_R,r_N,r_h,r_G,r_b\).  All undifferenced factors are bounded by the true and fitted margins.  In particular,
\[
 r_R+r_N+r_h+r_G+r_b\leq R_\Sigma,                              \tag{52}
\]
which proves the asserted \(O_P(R_\Sigma)\) relation.  Notice that neither \(r_{A,\infty}\) nor \(r_{Z,\infty}\) appears in (50)--(52); those two errors enter only the screening ratio \(\kappa_{\mathrm{supp},n}\).

Let \(\widehat b_{\widehat U}\) be the right-hand side formed from the same cleaned fitted law and \(\widehat U\).  Adding and subtracting one factor at a time gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
 &\widehat h^{\mathsf T}\widehat G_{\tau_G}^{\dagger}\widehat b_{\widehat U}
   -h^{\mathsf T}G^+b_U\\
 &=(\widehat h-h)^{\mathsf T}\widehat G_{\tau_G}^{\dagger}\widehat b_{\widehat U}
   +h^{\mathsf T}(\widehat G_{\tau_G}^{\dagger}-G^+)\widehat b_{\widehat U}
   +h^{\mathsf T}G^+(\widehat b_{\widehat U}-b_U).
\end{aligned}                                                    \tag{53}
\]
Conditional Cauchy--Schwarz, (51), and the uniform margin bounds imply
\[
 \|\widehat h^{\mathsf T}\widehat G_{\tau_G}^{\dagger}\widehat b_{\widehat U}
   -h^{\mathsf T}G^+b_U\|_2
 \leq C_{\mathrm{reg}}(r_h+r_G+r_b)
 \leq C_{\mathrm{reg}}R_\Sigma.                                \tag{54}
\]
Likewise, (48) and (50) imply
\[
 \|\widehat N\widehat U-N_BU\|_2
 \leq\|(\widehat N-N_B)\widehat U\|_2+\|N_B(\widehat U-U)\|_2
 \leq C_{\mathrm{reg}}R_\Sigma.                                \tag{55}
\]
Subtracting (54) from (55) according to the definitions of \(\widehat Q\) and \(Q\) proves
\[
 \|\widehat Q\widehat U-QU\|_2\leq C_{\mathrm{reg}}R_\Sigma. \tag{56}
\]
Finally,
\[
 (\widehat U-\widehat Q\widehat U)-(U-QU)
 =(\widehat U-U)-(\widehat Q\widehat U-QU),
\]
so (50), (56), and the triangle inequality prove the last assertion.

Fix one measurement view and suppress its subscript.  For a raw fitted probability column \(p=(p_1,\ldots,p_K)^{\mathsf T}\), define
\[
 q_a=p_a\mathbf 1\{p_a>\tau_{S,n}\},
 \qquad s=\sum_{b=1}^Kq_b,
 \qquad \bar p_a=q_a/s.                                         \tag{57}
\]
Because \(\sum_ap_a=1\), the deleted mass \(t=1-s\) satisfies \(0\leq t\leq K\tau_{S,n}\).  For \(\tau_{S,n}<1/(2K)\), which holds with probability tending to one because \(\tau_{S,n}\downarrow0\), we have \(s\geq1/2\).  Hence
\[
 |\bar p_a-p_a|
 \leq|q_a-p_a|+q_a\frac{1-s}{s}
 \leq\tau_{S,n}+2K\tau_{S,n}.                                 \tag{58}
\]
Applying (58) to every column of both views and using the triangle inequality gives
\[
 \|\bar M_A-M_A\|_\infty
 \leq r_{A,\infty}+(2K+1)\tau_{S,n},
 \qquad
 \|\bar M_Z-M_Z\|_\infty
 \leq r_{Z,\infty}+(2K+1)\tau_{S,n}.                           \tag{59}
\]
The same pointwise inequality followed by the conditional \(L^2(P)\) norm gives
\[
 \|\bar M_A-M_A\|_2\leq C_{\mathrm{reg}}(r_A+\tau_{S,n})
 =C_{\mathrm{reg}}r_A^c,
 \quad
 \|\bar M_Z-M_Z\|_2\leq C_{\mathrm{reg}}r_Z^c.               \tag{60}
\]

Define the analysis event
\[
 \mathcal E_{\mathrm{clean},n}
 =\{r_{A,\infty}+r_{Z,\infty}\leq\tau_{S,n}\}.               \tag{61}
\]
If \(M_A(x)_{aj}=0\), then on (61), \(\widehat M_A(x)_{aj}\leq\tau_{S,n}\), and (57) sets \(\bar M_A(x)_{aj}=0\).  The same argument applies to \(Z\).  Since
\[
 \frac{r_{A,\infty}+r_{Z,\infty}}{\tau_{S,n}}
 =\kappa_{\mathrm{supp},n}=o_P(1),                              \tag{62}
\]
the probability of (61) tends to one.  This establishes exact true-zero recovery.  The argument never lower-bounds a positive cell: a positive cell may also be deleted, and (58)--(60) already account for that deletion.

It remains to prove the conditional-zero bound.  Put \(\widehat B=\bar M_A\odot\bar M_Z\).  The fitted projector algebra gives
\(\widehat B^{\mathsf T}\widehat N=0\).  Both terms defining \(\widehat k=\widehat Q\widehat U\) lie in \(\operatorname{range}(\widehat N)\), including when the Gram inverse is spectrally thresholded, because every coordinate of \(\widehat h\) is an \(\widehat N\)-residual.  Therefore
\[
 \widehat B^{\mathsf T}\widehat k=0.                            \tag{63}
\]
Using \(d=Bw\), conditioning on \((Y,X)\), subtracting (63), and using \(g w_j=\pi_jf_j\) gives
\[
 E_P(\widehat k\mid X=x)
 =\sum_{j=1}^K\pi_j(x)\int_{\mathcal Y}f_j(y\mid x)
 \{B_{\cdot j}(x)-\widehat B_{\cdot j}(x)\}^{\mathsf T}
 \widehat k(y,x)d\nu(y).                                      \tag{64}
\]
Let \(\Delta_A=M_A-\bar M_A\) and \(\Delta_Z=M_Z-\bar M_Z\).  Columnwise tensor multiplication yields the exact identity
\[
 B_{\cdot j}-\widehat B_{\cdot j}
 =\Delta_{A,\cdot j}\otimes M_{Z,\cdot j}
  +M_{A,\cdot j}\otimes\Delta_{Z,\cdot j}
  -\Delta_{A,\cdot j}\otimes\Delta_{Z,\cdot j}.               \tag{65}
\]
The established tangent-space and finite-projector theorems imply
\[
 E_P(k\mid A,J,X)=0,
 \qquad E_P(k\mid Z,J,X)=0.                                   \tag{66}
\]
For example, if \(M_A(x)_{aj}>0\), three-view independence and the first equality in (66) imply
\[
 \int_{\mathcal Y}f_j(y\mid x)
 \sum_zM_Z(x)_{zj}k_{az}(y,x)d\nu(y)=0.                        \tag{67}
\]
If \(M_A(x)_{aj}=0\), exact recovery on \(\mathcal E_{\mathrm{clean},n}\) gives \(\Delta_A(x)_{aj}=0\).  Thus the term in (65) that is linear in \(\Delta_A\) vanishes after replacing \(\widehat k\) by \(k\), for every cell, and the symmetric assertion holds for the term linear in \(\Delta_Z\).

Write \(\widehat k=k+(\widehat k-k)\) in the two linear terms of (65) and keep \(\widehat k\) in the product term.  The true and fitted positivity and singular-value margins, bounded outcome, and
\(\|\widehat G_{\tau_G}^{\dagger}\|_{\mathrm{op}}\leq2/\varepsilon\) bound \(k\) and \(\widehat k\) uniformly.  Conditional Cauchy--Schwarz, (60), and integration over \(P_X\) now give
\[
 \|E_P\widehat k\|
 \leq C_{\mathrm{reg}}
 \left[(r_A^c+r_Z^c)\|\widehat k-k\|_2+r_A^cr_Z^c\right].      \tag{68}
\]
Equations (59)--(62) and (68) prove all assertions.

Work coordinatewise and set \(k=QU\) and \(\widehat k=\widehat Q\widehat U\).  By the support-cleaning conditional-zero lemma, \(\kappa_{\mathrm{supp},n}=o_P(1)\) produces an event \(\mathcal E_{\mathrm{clean},n}\) of probability tending to one on which
\[
 \|E_P\widehat k\|
 \leq C_{\mathrm{reg}}
 \left[(r_A^c+r_Z^c)\|\widehat k-k\|_2+r_A^cr_Z^c\right].       \tag{69}
\]
The cleaned score-stability lemma gives \(\|\widehat k-k\|_2\leq C_{\mathrm{reg}}R_\Sigma\).  Consequently,
\[
 \|E_P\widehat k\|
 \leq C_{\mathrm{reg}}
 \{(r_A^c+r_Z^c)R_\Sigma+r_A^cr_Z^c\}.                         \tag{70}
\]

We next calculate the raw bridge mean.  The bridges in \(\widehat U\) are formed from \(\bar M_A\) and \(\bar M_Z\).  For \(j,\ell\in\mathcal J\), define
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \delta^A_{j\ell}(X)
 &=E_P\{\bar a_j(A,X)\mid J=\ell,X\}-\mathbf 1\{j=\ell\},\\
 \delta^Z_{j\ell}(X)
 &=E_P\{\bar z_j(Z,X)\mid J=\ell,X\}-\mathbf 1\{j=\ell\}.
\end{aligned}                                                    \tag{71}
\]
The bridge definition and the true measurement laws give the exact matrix identities
\[
 \delta^A=\bar M_A^{-1}M_A-I_K=\bar M_A^{-1}(M_A-\bar M_A),
 \qquad
 \delta^Z=\bar M_Z^{-1}M_Z-I_K=\bar M_Z^{-1}(M_Z-\bar M_Z).     \tag{72}
\]
The cleaned fitted singular-value half-margins and the cleaning bounds imply
\[
 \|\delta^A\|_{L^2(P_X)}\leq C_{\mathrm{reg}}r_A^c,
 \qquad
 \|\delta^Z\|_{L^2(P_X)}\leq C_{\mathrm{reg}}r_Z^c,            \tag{73}
\]
and both matrices are uniformly bounded.

By three-view conditional independence, conditional on \((J=\ell,X)\), the factors \(Y,A,Z\) separate.  Since \(\widehat m_j(x)=\int y\widehat f_j(y\mid x)d\nu(y)\),
\(E_P(Y-\widehat m_j\mid J=\ell,X)=m_\ell-\widehat m_j\).  Expanding \(\widehat U_j\), conditioning first on \((J,X)\), and summing over \(J\) yields the exact equality
\[
\begin{aligned}
 E_P(\widehat U_j\mid X)-m_j
={}&(\widehat m_j-m_j)
 \left[1-\frac{\pi_j}{\widehat\pi_j}
 (1+\delta^A_{jj})(1+\delta^Z_{jj})\right]\\
&+\widehat\pi_j^{-1}\sum_{\ell\ne j}\pi_\ell
 \delta^A_{j\ell}\delta^Z_{j\ell}(m_\ell-\widehat m_j).       \tag{74}
\end{aligned}
\]
For \(\ell=j\), both bridge means equal one plus their errors; for \(\ell\ne j\), both indicator terms are zero, which proves (74) without approximation.

Latent positivity and the fitted propensity half-margin give \(\pi_j^{-1}\leq\varepsilon^{-1}\) and \(\widehat\pi_j^{-1}\leq2\varepsilon^{-1}\).  The declared common bounded support gives \(|m_\ell|\vee|\widehat m_j|\leq L\).  Also
\[
 \left|1-\frac{\pi_j}{\widehat\pi_j}\right|
 \leq2\varepsilon^{-1}|\widehat\pi_j-\pi_j|.                  \tag{75}
\]
Expanding the bracket in the first line of (74), using the uniform bounds on \(\delta^A,\delta^Z\), and applying Cauchy--Schwarz with (73) bounds its expectation by
\(C_{\mathrm{reg}}r_m(r_\pi+r_A^c+r_Z^c)\).  Cauchy--Schwarz applied to the second line of (74) bounds its expectation by \(C_{\mathrm{reg}}r_A^cr_Z^c\).  Since \(K\) is fixed and \(E_Pm_j(X)=\psi_j\),
\[
 \|E_P\widehat U-\psi\|
 \leq C_{\mathrm{reg}}
 \{r_m(r_\pi+r_A^c+r_Z^c)+r_A^cr_Z^c\}.                       \tag{76}
\]
Finally,
\[
 E_P(\widehat U-\widehat Q\widehat U)-\psi
 =(E_P\widehat U-\psi)-E_P\widehat k.
\]
Combining (70), (76), and the definition of \(\Delta_n\) proves the displayed bias bound on \(\mathcal E_{\mathrm{clean},n}\).

For the derivative assertions, let \(t\mapsto\eta_t\) be a support-preserving two-sided regular perturbation with \(\eta_0=\eta\), and evaluate the score mean under \(P=P_{\eta_0}\).  If only \(M_A\) varies, then \(m_t=m\), \(\pi_t=\pi\), and \(\delta_t^Z=0\).  Equation (74) gives
\[
 E_PU(\eta_t)-\psi=0.                                          \tag{77}
\]
Support preservation makes the true-zero discrepancy identically zero.  The conditional-zero calculation (64)--(68), with the \(Z\)-error equal to zero, gives
\[
 \|E_PQ(\eta_t)U(\eta_t)\|
 \leq C_{\mathrm{reg}}r_A(t)
 \|Q(\eta_t)U(\eta_t)-QU\|_2=O(t^2),                          \tag{78}
\]
because DQM differentiability gives \(r_A(t)=O(|t|)\), while the separated inverse and Gram-gap perturbation identities give score displacement \(O(|t|)\).  Equations (77)--(78) make the derivative at zero vanish.

If only \(f\) varies coherently, then \(M_A,M_Z,\pi\), and \(B\) are fixed, so \(\delta_t^A=\delta_t^Z=0\).  Equation (74) again gives \(E_PU(\eta_t)=\psi\).  Projector algebra gives \(B^{\mathsf T}N_t=0\), and each column of \(h_t=N_tc_t\) is in \(\ker(B^{\mathsf T})\); hence
\[
 B^{\mathsf T}\{Q_tU(\eta_t)\}=0.                             \tag{79}
\]
By three-view independence, the \(j\)-th coordinate of (79) is
\[
 E_P\{Q_tU(\eta_t)\mid Y,J=j,X\}
 =\sum_{a,z}B_{(a,z),j}\{Q_tU(\eta_t)\}_{az}(Y,X)=0.
\]
Iterated expectation gives \(E_PQ_tU(\eta_t)=0\) exactly.  Thus the mean bias is identically zero along the coherent \(f\)-only perturbation, proving the second derivative assertion.

For a training fold \(f\), define
\[
 S(O)=U(O)-QU(O)=\psi+\phi^{\mathrm{eff}}(O),
 \qquad
 \widehat S_f=\widehat U_f-\widehat Q_f\widehat U_f,             \tag{80}
\]
where every hatted object in \(\widehat S_f\) is computed from the cleaned product law.  Let \(n_f\) be the size of its held-out fold.  Adding and subtracting foldwise conditional means gives the exact decomposition
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \sqrt n(\widehat\psi-\psi)
={}&n^{-1/2}\sum_{i=1}^n\phi^{\mathrm{eff}}(O_i)\\
&+n^{-1/2}\sum_{f=1}^{F_{\mathrm{fold}}}
 \sum_{i:\,\mathrm{fold}(i)=f}
 \bigl[(\widehat S_f-S)(O_i)-P(\widehat S_f-S)\bigr]\\
&+n^{-1/2}\sum_{f=1}^{F_{\mathrm{fold}}}n_fP(\widehat S_f-\psi). \tag{81}
\end{aligned}
\]
Conditional on the training observations for fold \(f\), its held-out observations are independent of \(\widehat S_f\), and its centered summands have conditional second moment bounded by
\[
 \frac{n_f}{n}\|\widehat S_f-S\|_2^2.                          \tag{82}
\]
The cleaned score-stability lemma and \(R_\Sigma=o_P(1)\) make (82) converge to zero in probability.  Conditional Markov inequality and the fixed number of folds therefore make the middle two lines of (81) \(o_P(1)\).

The support-cleaning event has probability tending to one because \(\kappa_{\mathrm{supp},n}=o_P(1)\).  On that event the quadratic-bias lemma gives, foldwise,
\[
 \left\|n^{-1/2}\sum_fn_fP(\widehat S_f-\psi)\right\|
 \leq\sqrt n\,C_{\mathrm{reg}}\max_f\Delta_{n,f}=o_P(1).       \tag{83}
\]
The explicitly imposed condition \(\tau_{S,n}=o_P(n^{-1/4})\) covers training-fold-random thresholds and ensures that the cleaning contribution \(r_A^c-r_A=r_Z^c-r_Z=\tau_{S,n}\) lies in the required product-rate window; the actual bias conclusion in (83) is recorded by \(\Delta_n=o_P(n^{-1/2})\).  Equations (81)--(83) prove the asymptotic linear expansion.

The true regularity margins, bounded outcome, fixed \(K\), and the finite-projector and Gram-gap bounds make \(\phi^{\mathrm{eff}}\) bounded and centered.  For fixed \(t\in\mathbb R^K\), Taylor expansion of its characteristic function, with a bounded third-order remainder, gives
\[
 E_P\exp\{it^{\mathsf T}\phi^{\mathrm{eff}}/\sqrt n\}
 =1-\frac{t^{\mathsf T}V_{\mathrm{eff}}t}{2n}+o(n^{-1}).       \tag{84}
\]
Independence raises (84) to the \(n\)-th power, whose limit is
\(\exp\{-t^{\mathsf T}V_{\mathrm{eff}}t/2\}\).  Thus every scalar projection has the asserted normal limit, and the characteristic function identifies the joint limit as \(N(0,V_{\mathrm{eff}})\).  Combining this limit with the asymptotic linear expansion proves the second assertion.

For covariance consistency, score stability gives \(\widehat S_f\to S\) in \(L^2(P)\) for every fold.  The fitted half-margins, spectral cutoff, and bounded outcome make these scores uniformly bounded.  Conditional on the training data, a direct second-moment calculation therefore gives
\[
 \left\|P_{n,f}(\widehat S_f\widehat S_f^{\mathsf T})
 -P(\widehat S_f\widehat S_f^{\mathsf T})\right\|_{\mathrm F}=o_P(1). \tag{85}
\]
Cauchy--Schwarz gives
\[
 \|P(\widehat S_f\widehat S_f^{\mathsf T})-P(SS^{\mathsf T})\|_{\mathrm F}
 \leq\|\widehat S_f-S\|_2(\|\widehat S_f\|_2+\|S\|_2)=o_P(1). \tag{86}
\]
Summing the fixed number of folds and using the already proved consistency \(\widehat\psi\to_P\psi\) yields
\[
 \widehat V_{\mathrm{eff}}
 \to_P E_P\{(S-\psi)(S-\psi)^{\mathsf T}\}=V_{\mathrm{eff}},
\]
as required.

added_lemmas.statement:
Put \(D_0=d_X+1\), \(\rho_n=n^{-\beta/(2\beta+D_0)}\), and \(\zeta_n=\rho_n\sqrt{\log n}\).  If \(\beta>D_0/2\) and a label-aligned raw measurement fit satisfies
\[
 r_{A,\infty}+r_{Z,\infty}=O_P(\zeta_n),
 \qquad r_A+r_Z=O_P(\rho_n),
\]
then the deterministic choice
\[
 \tau_{S,n}=\{\zeta_n n^{-1/4}\}^{1/2}
\]
satisfies
\[
 \zeta_n=o(\tau_{S,n}),
 \qquad \tau_{S,n}=o(n^{-1/4}),
 \qquad \kappa_{\mathrm{supp},n}=o_P(1).
\]
For the threshold-and-renormalize cleaning, it also gives
\[
 r_A^c+r_Z^c=O_P(\rho_n+\tau_{S,n})=o_P(n^{-1/4}),
\]
and exact recovery of every true-zero measurement cell with probability tending to one, without a beta-min condition on positive cells.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
For every regular coherent foldwise fit, let \(\widehat M_A\) and \(\widehat M_Z\) denote the raw measurement fits and let \(\bar M_A\) and \(\bar M_Z\) denote their threshold-and-renormalize cleanings.  Every fitted bridge and every fitted object \(\widehat B,\widehat d,\widehat D,\widehat R,\widehat N,\widehat h,\widehat G,\widehat b_{(\cdot)},\widehat Q\) is formed from \((\bar M_A,\bar M_Z)\), and \(\widehat m_j(x)=\int_{\mathcal Y}y\widehat f_j(y\mid x)d\nu(y)\).  With \(r_A^c=r_A+\tau_{S,n}\) and \(r_Z^c=r_Z+\tau_{S,n}\),
\[
 \{E_P\|\widehat N-N_B\|_{\mathrm{op}}^2\}^{1/2}
 \leq C_{\mathrm{reg}}(r_D+r_B),
\]
\(r_R+r_N+r_h+r_G+r_b=O_P(R_\Sigma)\), and
\[
 \|\widehat Q\widehat U-QU\|_{L^2(P)}
 \leq C_{\mathrm{reg}}R_\Sigma.
\]
The full estimated efficient score \(\widehat U-\widehat Q\widehat U\) has the same linear \(L^2(P)\) stability bound relative to \(U-QU\).  In particular, the bridge perturbations use
\[
 \bar M_A^{-1}M_A-I_K=\bar M_A^{-1}(M_A-\bar M_A),
 \qquad
 \bar M_Z^{-1}M_Z-I_K=\bar M_Z^{-1}(M_Z-\bar M_Z),
\]
so the raw essential-supremum errors \(r_{A,\infty}\) and \(r_{Z,\infty}\) are screening quantities only, while \(r_B,\ldots,r_b\) are errors of the cleaned-law plug-ins.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The old claim and proof formed every hatted operator from the raw measurement fits.  That is incompatible with the mandated support cleaning and makes the inverse-feature perturbation use the wrong matrix.  The replacement restricts the result to the coherent cleaned-law construction, distinguishes raw screening errors from cleaned errors, and derives the score bound with the cleaned rates.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
At every two-sided pathwise-interior \(P\in\mathcal M_{K,\varepsilon}\), consider a foldwise coherent fit.  Let \(\widehat M_A,\widehat M_Z\) be the raw measurement fits and \(\bar M_A,\bar M_Z\) their threshold-and-renormalize cleanings.  If \(\kappa_{\mathrm{supp},n}=o_P(1)\), then with probability tending to one every true-zero measurement cell is exactly zero in the corresponding cleaned matrix.  No lower bound on the positive entries of \(M_A\) or \(M_Z\) is required.  Moreover,
\[
 \|\bar M_A-M_A\|_\infty\leq C_{\mathrm{reg}}(r_{A,\infty}+\tau_{S,n}),
 \qquad
 \|\bar M_Z-M_Z\|_\infty\leq C_{\mathrm{reg}}(r_{Z,\infty}+\tau_{S,n}),
\]
and the analogous conditional \(L^2(P)\) bounds are \(C_{\mathrm{reg}}r_A^c\) and \(C_{\mathrm{reg}}r_Z^c\).  If \(k=QU\) and \(\widehat k=\widehat Q\widehat U\), coordinatewise, with all hatted derived objects formed from the cleaned matrices, then on the same event
\[
 \|E_P\widehat k\|
 \leq C_{\mathrm{reg}}\left[
 (r_A^c+r_Z^c)\|\widehat k-k\|_{L^2(P)}+r_A^cr_Z^c
 \right].
\]
Thus support cleaning removes the former first-order leakage term.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The diagnostic-only version retained additive first-order leakage. \[
 r_\pi+r_A+r_Z+r_f=O_P(\rho_n),
 \qquad \rho_n=n^{-\beta/(2\beta+d_X+1)}.
\]
Second, with \(\zeta_n=\rho_n\sqrt{\log n}\),
\[
 \|\widehat\pi-\pi\|_\infty+
 \|\widehat M_A-M_A\|_\infty+
 \|\widehat M_Z-M_Z\|_\infty+
 \|\widehat f-f\|_\infty=O_P(\zeta_n).
\]
Third, the empirical minimum modal-gap rule over the \(K!\) common permutations selects the population labeling with probability tending to one. The cleaned support-rate-window lemma proves that such a threshold is compatible with the stated smoothness and yields exact true-zero recovery.  What remains open is the likelihood-curvature, spline approximation, localization, and uniform-rate proof for this specifically prescribed global product-likelihood fit; no conclusion about \(R_\Sigma\) or \(\Delta_n\) is asserted merely from a list of coordinatewise \(L^2\) rates.
